title: “A conspiracy of her prophets” — the Brenton Greek says her princes
summary: The KJV says “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion”. The Hebrew prints קֶשֶׁר נְבִיאֶיהָ, “conspiracy of her prophets”. Brenton’s Greek prints οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι, “those who lead”, which Brenton’s English renders “princes”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Ezekiel 22:25: “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls; they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 22:25: קֶ֤שֶׁר נְבִיאֶ֙יהָ֙ בְּתֹוכָ֔הּ כַּאֲרִ֥י שֹׁואֵ֖ג טֹ֣רֵֽף טָ֑רֶף נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָכָ֗לוּ חֹ֤סֶן וִיקָר֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ אַלְמְנֹותֶ֖יהָ הִרְבּ֥וּ בְתֹוכָֽהּ׃ [a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing prey, they devoured life, took treasure and precious things, made her widows many in her midst]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 22:25: Ἧς οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ὡς λέοντες ὠρυόμενοι ἁρπάζοντες ἁρπάγματα, ψυχὰς κατεσθίοντες ἐν δυναστείᾳ, καὶ τιμὰς λαμβάνοντες· καὶ χῆραί σου ἐπληθύνθησαν ἐν μέσῳ σου. Brenton English Ezekiel 22:25: “whose princes in the midst of her are as roaring lions seizing prey, devouring souls by oppression, and taking bribes; and thy widows are multiplied in the midst of thee.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK22.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/22/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK22.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK22.htm.

KJV Ezekiel 22:25: “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls; they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof.” Hebrew (WLC) 22:25: קֶ֤שֶׁר נְבִיאֶ֙יהָ֙ בְּתֹוכָ֔הּ כַּאֲרִ֥י שֹׁואֵ֖ג טֹ֣רֵֽף טָ֑רֶף נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָכָ֗לוּ חֹ֤סֶן וִיקָר֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ אַלְמְנֹותֶ֖יהָ הִרְבּ֥וּ בְתֹוכָֽהּ׃ Brenton’s Greek 22:25: Ἧς οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ὡς λέοντες ὠρυόμενοι ἁρπάζοντες ἁρπάγματα, ψυχὰς κατεσθίοντες ἐν δυναστείᾳ, καὶ τιμὰς λαμβάνοντες· καὶ χῆραί σου ἐπληθύνθησαν ἐν μέσῳ σου. [Whose leaders in the midst of her are like roaring lions seizing prey, devouring souls by power, and taking honours; and your widows were multiplied in the midst of you] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK22.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/22/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK22.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew subject is a conspiracy belonging to her prophets (נְבִיאֶיהָ), the KJV’s word. The Brenton Greek has a plural participle meaning leaders or rulers, and has no word for prophets or for a conspiracy; its first clause begins with the relative “whose”. The prophets are then named again in the next verses (22:28), so both texts mention prophets in the passage, but not in this clause.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted has קֶשֶׁר נְבִיאֶיהָ בְּתוֹכָהּ, “a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst”. The Greek printed at the same verse has οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι, “the leaders”, and no word for conspiracy. Verse 28 of the same chapter, in both texts, still has the prophets daubing and prophesying lies, so the two texts differ on who is likened to a lion at 22:25.

title: “Ye eat with the blood … ye stand upon your sword” — the Brenton Greek page does not print these clauses
summary: The KJV has two charges against those left in the waste places: eating with the blood and lifting eyes to idols (33:25) and standing on the sword, working abomination and defiling a neighbour’s wife (33:26). The Hebrew prints both verses in full. Brenton’s Greek page ends verse 25 after “therefore say to them, Thus saith the Lord God” and prints no verse 26; its next verse, 27, begins at “As I live”.

title: “The east country … the desert” — the Brenton Greek prints Galilee and Arabia
summary: The KJV says the waters “issue out toward the east country, and go down into the desert”. The Hebrew prints אֶל־הַגְּלִילָה הַקַּדְמוֹנָה … עַל־הָעֲרָבָה, “to the district (Galilah) eastward … upon the Arabah”. Brenton’s Greek prints τὴν Γαλιλαίαν τὴν πρὸς ἀνατολάς … τὴν Ἀραβίαν, “Galilee that lies eastward … Arabia”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Ezekiel 47:8: “Then said he unto me, These waters issue out toward the east country, and go down into the desert, and go into the sea: which being brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 47:8: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּ֤יִם הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יֹוצְאִ֗ים אֶל־הַגְּלִילָה֙ הַקַּדְמֹונָ֔ה וְיָרְד֖וּ עַל־הָֽעֲרָבָ֑ה וּבָ֣אוּ הַיָּ֔מָּה אֶל־הַיָּ֥מָּה הַמּֽוּצָאִ֖ים [וְנִרְפְּאוּ כ] (וְנִרְפּ֥וּ ק) הַמָּֽיִם׃ [These waters go out toward the eastern district, and go down to the Arabah, and enter the sea, the sea of the outflowing; the waters shall be healed]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 47:8: Καὶ εἶπε πρὸν μὲ, τὸ ὕδωρ τοῦτο τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν τὴν πρὸς ἀνατολὰς, καὶ κατέβαινεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἀραβίαν, καὶ ἤρχετο ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τὸ ὕδωρ τῆς διεκβολῆς, καὶ ὑγιάσει τὰ ὕδατα· Brenton English Ezekiel 47:8: “And he said to me, This is the water that goes forth to Galilee that lies eastward, and it is gone down to Arabia, and has reached as far as to the sea to the outlet of the water: and it shall heal the waters.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK47.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/47/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK47.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK47.htm.

reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The KJV puts ordinary words, “east country” and “desert”, where the Greek prints the place names Galilee and Arabia. A reader of the KJV does not see either name; a reader of the Greek sees both.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted has אֶל־הַגְּלִילָה הַקַּדְמוֹנָה, “to the eastern region” (גְּלִילָה, a district or circuit, from the same root as the name Galilee), and עַל־הָעֲרָבָה, “down to the Arabah”, the rift valley or steppe. The KJV renders both as common nouns, “east country” and “desert”. The Greek printed at the same verse renders both as place names, Galilee and Arabia, so the two texts present the waters as flowing toward named regions and the KJV as flowing toward unnamed ones.

title: Ezekiel bears his baggage “upon thy shoulders” — the Brenton Greek has him lifted up on others’ shoulders
summary: In the sign of the exile the KJV has Ezekiel carry his baggage on his own shoulder through the hole in the wall (12:6, 12:7). The Hebrew prints עַל־כָּתֵף תִּשָּׂא, “on a shoulder you shall carry”, and עַל־כָּתֵף נָשָׂאתִי, “on a shoulder I carried”. Brenton’s Greek prints ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀναληφθήσῃ, “thou shalt be taken up on shoulders”, and ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀνελήφθην, “I was taken up on shoulders”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Ezekiel 12:6: “In their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders, and carry it forth in the twilight: thou shalt cover thy face, that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 12:6: לְעֵ֨ינֵיהֶ֜ם עַל־כָּתֵ֤ף תִּשָּׂא֙ בָּעֲלָטָ֣ה תֹוצִ֔יא פָּנֶ֣יךָ תְכַסֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־מֹופֵ֥ת נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ [before their eyes you shall carry it on a shoulder, you shall bring it out in the dark; you shall cover your face, and not see the ground]. title: “Hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword” — Brenton’s Greek prints “laid wait craftily for the house of Israel”

text: KJV Ezekiel 35:5: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:” Hebrew (WLC) 35:5: יַ֗עַן הֱיֹ֤ות לְךָ֙ אֵיבַ֣ת עֹולָ֔ם וַתַּגֵּ֥ר אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל־יְדֵי־חָ֑רֶב בְּעֵ֣ת אֵידָ֔ם בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֹ֥ן קֵֽץ׃ Brenton’s Greek 35:5: Ἀντὶ τοῦ γενέσθαι σε ἐχθρὰν αἰωνίαν, καὶ ἐνεκάθισας τῷ οἴκῳ Ἰσραὴλ δόλῳ, ἐν χειρὶ ἐχθρῶν μαχαίρᾳ ἐν καιρῷ ἀδικίας, ἐπʼ ἐσχάτων. [Because you have been an everlasting enemy, and you lay in wait for the house of Israel with guile, by the hand of enemies with a sword, in a time of injustice, at the last] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK35.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/35/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK35.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has וַתַּגֵּר אֶת־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־יְדֵי־חָרֶב, which the KJV renders “hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword”. The Greek printed at the same verse has a verb for sitting or lying in wait and the noun δόλῳ, “guile”, in place of any pouring out or blood. The two texts describe different actions by Edom against Israel, one of killing and one of ambush, though both end with a sword.
scope: T applies at Ezekiel 35:5 only. The Hebrew verb is rare and its sense is debated, and the KJV’s “blood” is its interpretation of the word; the record sets out what the texts print and does not claim the KJV departs from the Hebrew. This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. The Greek quoted is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original, and the record does not claim the Greek is a mistranslation of the Hebrew. title: “As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel… so will I do unto thee” — Brenton’s Greek does not print the clause
summary: The KJV of Ezekiel 35:15 says that as Edom rejoiced at the inheritance of Israel because it was desolate, so the Lord will do to Edom. Brenton’s Greek begins at the next clause, Ἔρημον ἔσῃ ὄρος Σηεὶρ, “you shall be desolate, mount Seir”, and ends “you shall know that I am the Lord their God”.
text: KJV Ezekiel 35:15: “As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it: and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Hebrew (WLC) 35:15: כְּשִׂמְחָ֨תְךָ֜ לְנַחְלַ֧ת בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמֵ֖מָה כֵּ֣ן אֶעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֑ךְ שְׁמָמָ֨ה תִֽהְיֶ֤ה הַר־שֵׂעִיר֙ וְכָל־אֱדֹ֣ום כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ Brenton’s Greek 35:15: Ἔρημον ἔσῃ ὄρος Σηεὶρ, καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰδουμαία, καὶ ἐξαναλωθήσεται, καὶ γνώσῃ ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς αὐτῶν. [You shall be desolate, mount Seir, and all Idumea, and it shall be utterly consumed; and you shall know that I am the Lord their God] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK35.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/35/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK35.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted opens with כְּשִׂמְחָתְךָ לְנַחֲלַת בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמֵמָה כֵּן אֶעֱשֶׂה־לָּךְ, “as your rejoicing at the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so I will do to you”. The Greek printed at the same verse has no matching clause. Where the Hebrew ends “they shall know that I am the Lord”, the Greek ends “you shall know that I am the Lord their God”, with a second-person verb and an added noun.

title: “Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads” — Brenton’s Greek prints “nor strip their hair bare; they shall cover their heads”
summary: In the KJV of Ezekiel 44:20 the priests do not shave their heads or let the locks grow long and only poll them. Brenton’s Greek has οὐ ψιλώσουσι, “they shall not strip bare”, for the hair, and καλύπτοντες καλύψουσιν τὰς κεφαλὰς, “covering they shall cover their heads”.
text: KJV Ezekiel 44:20: “Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads.” Hebrew (WLC) 44:20: וְרֹאשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ וּפֶ֖רַע לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ כָּסֹ֥ום יִכְסְמ֖וּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek 44:20: Καὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν οὐ ξυρήσονται, καὶ τὰς κόμας αὐτῶν οὐ ψιλώσουσι, καλύπτοντε καλύψουσιν τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν. [And they shall not shave their heads, nor strip their hair bare; covering they shall cover their heads] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK44.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/44/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK44.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has כָּסוֹם יִכְסְמוּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶם, “they shall surely trim their heads”, with a verb the KJV renders “poll” (cut short). It also has וּפֶרַע לֹא יְשַׁלֵּחוּ, “and they shall not let the locks go free”. The Greek printed at the same verse has καλύπτω, “to cover”, in place of a verb of cutting, and a verb for baring the hair in place of letting it grow. The instruction for the hair is trimming in the Hebrew and covering in the Greek.
